definition: A measured inventory and re-run of the stated hotspot method on what this checkout can support. The rental file (215,469 rows, 2021-01..2026-10, no coordinate columns) is joined on uppercased (block, street_name) to the sale-side geocode table's joinable keys (11,500 of its 11,637 distinct keys carry non-null lat/lon); inside the gate-pinned window 39,385 of 39,478 rows join (99.7644%) and the 93 unmatched rows are reported as a population. The stated method is re-run on that joined population: H3 resolution 8, median monthly_rent per cell, Getis-Ord Gi* with 99 seeded permutations over KNN k=8 row-standardised weights. Because the legacy does not state which z output its thresholds apply to, both esda z bases are reported (analytic Zs: no cell above any legacy threshold; simulation z_sim: 12 cells above 2.58) and neither is adjudicated as the legacy reading — that is an underspecification record, not a reproduction claim. Two of the legacy's six named areas have zero rows in this population and the other four's measured town-level medians differ from the legacy levels. Persistence is not measurable here: one gate-pinned period, no transition implementation, no artefact. The transaction-activity product is read read-only, carries zero rental tokens by token scan, and receives nothing; this study's result is written to a NEW rental-only asset. What this pack does NOT establish: the origin of any legacy number (no artefact is linked to them in either direction), any transition probability, and any claim about areas this population does not contain.

pSimFloor.semantics: esda G_Local p_sim is the smaller of the two permutation tails with a +1 correction (larger = sims >= G, flipped when the lower tail is smaller; p_sim = (larger+1)/(permutations+1)); with 99 permutations its floor is 1/100 = 0.01, so '99% confidence' maps to p_sim <= 0.01 and nothing smaller is attainable
